data.title: OpenAI Partnership Puts Conversational AI in Mattel Toys
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: Mattel与OpenAI合作，计划将人工智能融入其标志性玩具，如芭比和风火轮。通过生成式AI工具，设计师能快速创建新角色和场景，而原型则在虚拟环境中测试。AI让玩具更智能，能根据孩子的喜好进行调整，例如记住喜欢的睡前故事。然而，这一举措引发了一些家长和隐私保护者的担忧，尤其是鉴于Mattel之前涉及隐私问题的失败尝试（“Hello Barbie”）。尽管Mattel承诺加强隐私保护，但具体细节仍不明确，监管机构也保持警惕。AI玩具的潜力巨大，但也可能削弱无拘无束的想象力游戏。对于Mattel而言，这次合作既是机遇也是挑战，成功的关键在于赢得信任。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：将AI融入毛绒玩具的构想及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **[vunderba]** 认为将AI融入毛绒玩具的想法并非新事物，可以追溯到1980年代Axlon的AG "Talking" Bear。该评论强调了这种概念的历史背景，并通过提供一个历史产品链接来支持其观点。

• **[rooftopzen]** 持反对意见，认为这是一个糟糕的想法，并预测传统玩具公司高管可能会误解AI的细微差别。该评论通过引用一篇心理学文章来支持其担忧，指出潜在的管理和理解问题。

• **[add-sub-mul-div]** 提出一个有趣的观点，认为由于LLM（大型语言模型）对小孩子来说可能没有神秘感，因为他们从小就接触这些技术，所以他们可能对这种新奇事物最不感兴趣。该评论强调了技术普及对儿童吸引力的可能影响。

• **[CamperBob2]** 表达了对AI技术快速发展的担忧，提到我们已经接近能够制造出如斯皮尔伯格电影《AI》中那样的机器人熊。该评论提出了一个伦理思考，指出我们在技术发展时应考虑是否应该这样做。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI技术应用于毛绒玩具的可行性和伦理问题。一方认为这是技术进步的自然延伸，另一方则担心理解和管理上的挑战以及伦理问题。

• 讨论中引用的历史产品和心理学文章为各自观点提供了支持，展示了不同角度的思考。

• 技术普及对不同世代的影响也是一个值得注意的讨论点，尤其是对从小接触这些技术的小孩的影响。

Barbie Gets a Brain: OpenAI Partnership Puts Conversational AI in Mattel Toys
By
PYMNTS
|
June 28, 2025
|
Hot Wheels
and
Barbie’s Dreamhouse
just got a software update.
Get the Full Story
Complete the form to unlock this article and enjoy unlimited free access to all PYMNTS content — no additional logins required.

Subscribe to our daily newsletter, PYMNTS Today.
By completing this form, you agree to receive marketing communications from PYMNTS and to the sharing of your information with our sponsor, if applicable, in accordance with our
Privacy Policy
and
Terms and Conditions
.
Δ
Mattel
, the toy giant that has been shaping childhoods for generations, announced in a June 12
press release
a headline-grabbing partnership with
OpenAI
. The plan is to bake artificial intelligence into the DNA of Mattel’s most iconic toys, from Barbie to Hot Wheels. The move is bold, futuristic and, in the eyes of some parents and privacy advocates, somewhat unnerving.
In Mattel’s design studios, AI is already
revolutionizing
how toys
are imagined
. Designers feed prompts into
generative AI tools
, conjuring up dozens of new characters and playsets in the time it used to take to sketch one.
Prototypes
are tested
in virtual sandboxes. The result? Toys that are smarter, more responsive and — thanks to machine learning — capable of adapting to each child’s quirks and preferences.
Picture a
Barbie
that remembers your child’s favorite bedtime story or a Hot Wheels track that suggests new stunts based on your kid’s latest obsession. For Mattel, AI isn’t just about making toys talk; it’s about making them truly listen.
However, as Mattel races to reimagine playtime, it’s also running headlong into a new kind of parental anxiety. The company’s previous experiment with AI, the much-maligned “
Hello Barbie
,” fizzled after
revelations
that the doll recorded and uploaded children’s conversations. Now, as Mattel courts OpenAI’s conversational prowess, parents want assurances that
privacy won’t be sacrificed
for novelty.
This time, Mattel is promising transparency and robust data protections.
“As a central part of this collaboration, Mattel and OpenAI will emphasize safety, privacy and security in the products and experiences that come to market,” Mattel said in the press release.
But specifics are thin, and
watchdogs
are circling. In a world where a child’s first confidant might be a chatbot, the stakes for trust have never been higher.
Still, the possibilities are tantalizing. AI-powered toys could become tutors, coaches and creative collaborators — helping kids learn languages, solve puzzles or even script their own adventures.
Some
educators
see
AI as
a chance
to level the playing field,
offering
personalized learning to children who might otherwise be left behind.
Yet, there’s a risk that the magic of unstructured, imaginative play could get crowded out by algorithmic nudges. Will a generation raised on AI companions know how to invent their own games, or will they wait for the
next
prompt?
For Mattel, the gamble is existential. Get it right, and the company will set the standard for a new era of interactive play. Get it wrong, and it risks alienating the very families it hopes to enchant.
There’s a lesson here for anyone navigating the digital economy
—
including the world of banking and FinTech.
As AI weaves itself into the fabric of daily life, the rules of engagement are
being rewritten
. Transparency isn’t a nice-to-have; it’s table stakes. The brands that win will be the ones that build trust, not just features.
So, as Barbie gets an AI brain — and maybe a conscience — one thing is clear: The future of play is up for grabs. And this time, the kids aren’t the only ones watching.

• [nablaxcroissant] 指出这似乎是一个视觉系统的问题，LIDAR（激光雷达）在这种情况下可能无法提供帮助。他认为在平坦且空旷的道路上，主要依赖车道线作为视觉特征，这是特斯拉应该擅长的领域。尽管如此，特斯拉的表现仍不理想，但他认为过分强调LIDAR问题是不必要的。

• [ncr100] 关注的是如何让美国国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）介入并阻止这种测试，显示出对自动驾驶技术测试的潜在安全隐患的严重关切。

• 争议的焦点在于特斯拉自动驾驶系统的可靠性和安全性，特别是在城市道路测试中对其他交通参与者的潜在威胁。
• 对LIDAR在自动驾驶系统中的作用存在不同看法，有些人认为这不是LIDAR的问题，而是视觉系统的问题。
• 另一个值得注意的点是如何通过监管机构（如NTSB）来规范和监督自动驾驶技术的测试，以确保公共安全。

主要讨论点：社会问题背后的根本原因以及如何解决个人和社会的幸福感缺失

不同观点：

• [rramadass] 从哲学角度出发，引用了尼采的观点，认为人类追求的不是幸福，而是意义和目的。他指出科学革命颠覆了传统的社会结构，使人们失去了原有的认知框架，导致认知失调和不幸福。他的解决方案是结合现代科学和古代哲学（如印度教、佛教、希腊文化）来构建一个既客观又主观的理解框架，以解决幸福感缺失的问题。

补充讨论：
• [vannevar] 强调经济体系的影响，特别是资本主义对社会结构的破坏作用。他认为当前的盈利性系统缺乏人文关怀，使得人们难以找到社会支持。

• [rramadass] 则更关注哲学和认知层面的问题，强调重建认知框架的重要性。他认为通过融合科学和哲学，可以为人们提供一个更具意义和目的的生活方式，从而解决现代社会中的不幸福问题。

争议焦点：
• 两种观点的争议焦点在于社会问题根源的认定。[vannevar] 侧重于经济体系和资本主义对社会结构的破坏，而 [rramadass] 则更关注哲学和认知层面的问题，认为缺乏意义和目的感是根本原因。

• 解决方案的分歧：[vannevar] 主张通过改革经济体系来恢复社会结构，而 [rramadass] 则提倡通过哲学和科学的结合来重建认知框架。

这两种观点虽然出发点不同，但都指向了现代社会中人们缺乏幸福感和归属感的问题，提供了不同的分析和解决方案。

44408583.article_content:
What Went Wrong with Our Happiness
Jarek Orzel
7 min read
·
Just now
--
Listen
Share
Photo by
D Jonez
on
Unsplash
We live in the most prosperous era in human history, yet rates of depression, anxiety, and suicide continue to climb. Despite unprecedented resources and freedoms, we seem to be getting worse at the fundamental task of being happy. How did we arrive at this paradox?
Several years ago, I was convinced I could forge my path — one that would be better than my parents’. I believed my life would be more meaningful and enjoyable if I just applied enough intelligence and effort to optimize everything. The more years that have passed, the more humble I’ve become about how difficult it is to improve upon years of tradition and accumulated wisdom.
This personal journey reflects three broader cultural mistakes we’ve made, each feeding into the others like sides of the same coin: our arrogance toward tradition, our embrace of postmodern relativism, and our worship of the self. Together, they’ve created a perfect storm of unhappiness.
Arrogance: The Belief We Can Outsmart Tradition
Photo by
Alexander Ugolkov
on
Unsplash
Unteachable Lessons
Some of life’s most important lessons cannot be learned analytically — they must be experienced firsthand. We cannot learn through reading or reasoning that money doesn’t bring happiness; we must arrive at being wealthy and feel its limits. We cannot understand the loneliness of prioritizing career over relationships until we’re successful and alone. Some truths can only be achieved by experience, by becoming a different person entirely. These are unteachable lessons.
Yet we’ve developed a peculiar form of intellectual arrogance, believing we can shortcut this process by simply being smarter or more analytical than previous generations. We think our life path can be special and unique, that we can abandon the whole tradition and avoid the painful experiences that taught others these lessons. We’ll do better this time.
This reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of how knowledge works. Not everything can be solved through rational thinking alone. We operate based on insight versus inference, carrying intrinsic assumptions about the world and the outcomes of actions that we’re not even aware of. We excel at identifying biases in others but struggle when evaluating our own. Despite this, we persist in believing we’re the best judges of what’s good for us.
Since we can’t learn these lessons rationally, and we’re too arrogant to accept that others’ experiences apply to us, we’ve tried to create our own frameworks for meaning and purpose. But here’s where the problem compounds: our approach to meaning has become fundamentally egocentric. Meaningful life requires coherence, purpose, and significance (I strongly recommend this insightful
Modern Wisdom podcast episode with John Vervaeke
) — but we’ve twisted these into ‘for me, by me, to me’ versions that fail to provide genuine connection and orientation.
This egocentric approach leads us to focus on what is most visible and immediate in our personal scorekeeping — career achievements, material possessions, personal accomplishments. The value of relationships, by contrast, is ephemeral and hard to quantify, so we systematically undervalue them in our life planning.
We’ve forgotten that life happens in stages, each with its requirements and rewards. What makes sense at 25 may be disastrous at 45, but our culture pushes us to optimize for the immediate and visible rather than the long-term and relational.
Postmodernism Disease: When Everything Becomes Relative
Photo by
Jon Tyson
on
Unsplash
Here’s where things get particularly twisted. We are progressive — we believe in science, in progress, in human improvement. But we’ve simultaneously embraced postmodern assumptions that everything is relative and that no truth exists in the world. We’ve lost the stable values that previous generations called virtues.
The Collapse of Shared Standards
We’ve stopped believing that people should strive for certain virtues or ways of living. Instead, we’ve adopted the stance that everyone can live as they want. As a community, we cannot correct harmful behaviors. We’ve lost the concept of shame. Everything goes if it’s someone’s choice of life.
Consider how we can no longer contemplate OnlyFans models as representing a harmful way of living, because everyone has the right to decide about their life. We’ve created a world where community standards and moral guidance have been replaced by radical individualism disguised as tolerance. Any attempt to suggest that some ways of living are better than others is immediately dismissed as judgmental or oppressive.
Truth Becomes “What Works for Me”
We’ve lost the ability to recognize that some things work for individuals in the short term while being destructive to both the individual and society in the long term. Religion, for instance, demonstrably “works” for human flourishing in ways that our secular alter

data.title: "What LLVM Claims, but Fails to Deliver"
data.author: achierius
data.article_summary: 文章主要揭示了LLVM的Clang编译器的多个问题和缺陷，包括生成未优化或错误代码、整数除法和溢出检查的整数乘法例程性能低下等。作者批评LLVM在其编译器运行时库中声称提供高度优化的低级代码支持例程，但实际上却交付了未优化和低效的代码。文章通过多个例子展示了具体问题，如违反微软调用约定、128÷128位和64÷64位整数除法性能差、生成的机器代码无效等。作者还指出，这些问题严重影响了Clang编译器及其优化器的性能，并浪费了系统资源。文章最后建议开发者应更关注CPU时间的有效利用，而不仅仅是开发时间的减少。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：作者在网站上列出GCC和LLVM相关问题的目的和方式

不同观点：
• labrador认为该网站可能存在钓鱼风险，因此没有继续访问。这表明了对网站安全性或合法性的担忧。
• 12_throw_away提到作者似乎喜欢撰写关于编译器输出的争议性文章，但对作者具体不满的内容不甚清楚，暗示作者的批评可能缺乏明确的目标或重点。
• rcxdude质疑作者只是简单地将这些问题列在网站上，而不是向LLVM报告漏洞。同时，他们对作者在一些简单功能上添加版权声明以及页面底部的服务条款表示困惑和不满，认为这可能对LLVM贡献者产生负面影响。

补充讨论：
• 作者在处理GCC和LLVM相关技术问题时的方法和态度引起了一些读者的不解和批评。
• 网站的安全性（labrador提到的钓鱼风险）和内容合法性（rcxdude提到的版权声明和服务条款）成为讨论的附加焦点。
• 争议焦点在于作者行为的合理性以及其对开源社区的潜在影响。

这些观点共同构成了对作者处理技术问题方式的广泛质疑，涉及安全、版权和开源贡献实践等多个方面。

• 作者在处理GCC和LLVM相关技术问题时的方法和态度引起了一些读者的不解和批评。

data.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Mathematical Experiments
data.author: belter
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提出将数学视为一种通过计算探索模式的实验科学，并讨论了AI辅助证明系统对这一视角的影响。文章从Voevodsky的信心危机谈起，指出数学并非发现永恒真理，而是通过计算实验构建理论。数学真理不在于对应柏拉图式的现实，而在于成功预测计算结果；矛盾表明理论失败而非逻辑不可能。这一框架解释了为何直觉常超越严谨、为何需要多种框架来描述同一现象（多元主义），以及为何数学在物理学中“异常有效”。文章认为，数学的理解在于使用中的一致性，而非从公理推导。

Mathematics > History and Overview
arXiv:2506.19787
(math)
[Submitted on 24 Jun 2025]
Title:
The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Mathematical Experiments: What Makes Mathematics Work
Authors:
Asvin G
View a PDF of the paper titled The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Mathematical Experiments: What Makes Mathematics Work, by Asvin G
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
This essay proposes a reconceptualization of mathematics as an experimental science exploring patterns in computation and what the advent of AI-assited provers might imply in light of this reconceptualization. Beginning with Voevodsky's crisis of confidence, where a major result remained in limbo for 24 years, neither proven nor refuted, we argue that mathematics is not the discovery of eternal truths but theory-building in response to computational experiments. Just as physicists build theories to explain patterns in physical measurements, mathematicians build axiomatic frameworks to explain patterns observed through calculation and proof. In this view, mathematical truth is not about correspondence to platonic reality but about successful prediction of computational outcomes; contradictions indicate failed theories rather than logical impossibilities. This framework dissolves longstanding puzzles: it explains why intuition often outpaces rigor, why multiple frameworks are often necessary to capture the same phenomena (pluralism), and why mathematics is "unreasonably effective" in physics. Understanding mathematics as an experimental science illuminates both its power and its limits, suggesting that consistency in use, rather than deduction from axioms, is the true marker of mathematical understanding.

Photograph: Julian Anderson/The Guardian
View image in fullscreen

Photograph: Julian Anderson/The Guardian
Art
‘I was living in Doodle Land and didn’t know how to get back’: the million-dollar artist who drew himself crazy
As Mr Doodle, Sam Cox found a global audience and made a fortune with his signature scrawls covering furniture, clothes – and eventually an entire house. But behind the scenes, he was unravelling into psychosis
Michael Segalov
Sat 28 Jun 2025 06.45 EDT
Share
F
rom the road, it’s barely visible; glimpsed, maybe, if peered at with cheeks pressed against the property’s imposing iron gates. There is otherwise little out of the ordinary in this quiet Kent corner of London’s affluent commuter belt – St Michael’s has a village hall, a country club, a farm shop. But at the end of a snaking, hedge-lined driveway is an incongruous home: a sprawling, six-bedroom neo-Georgian mansion, almost every inch, inside and out, covered in the trademark black-on-white line drawings of its owner, Mr Doodle, the 31-year-old artist Sam Cox.
A car honks twice behind me. A woman in her 80s steps out. “It’s mindblowing, isn’t it?” Sam’s grandmother Sue says, eyebrows aloft. “And terribly … different.” The gates ahead buzz open. “Take it slowly,” she offers, by way of warning. “You’ll want to give your eyes a few minutes to adjust.”
Corner turned, the house comes into unobstructed view: an imposing modern manor enveloped floor to roof in lines, curves and cartoon-ish characters. All exterior walls are doodled over: statues, plant pots, phone box, chimney, guttering and window sashes, too. Standing in the doodled doorway to greet me are Sam and his artist wife Alena, 35, both in full doodle dress-up. “I sometimes say it’s like graffiti spaghetti,” Sam says of his style, inviting me to step over the doodled doormat. “It’s influenced by early-era New York street art, but intertwined, overlapping and cartoonish.” Six-foot-something Sam is gentle and softly spoken – most animated when talking about his work.
He’s joined by younger brother Tom – now Sam’s manager – and mum Andrea. Dad Neill and grandpa David are also on the payroll, today tasked with entertaining Sam and Alena’s two-year-old son Alfie. Having first found success in viral videos during the late 2010s, Sam’s various artistic ventures now earn significant sums: during one nine-month period in 2020, his artwork racked up $4.7m in sales – one piece fetched nearly $1m. That year, he was the world’s fifth most successful artist aged under 40 at auction.
Sam purchased his St Michael’s property for £1.35m in 2019. Its evolution from rural residence to live-in illustrated installation was the realisation of an ambition held for a decade. “I must have been 15 when I first planned it,” he says. “I was set a project called Obsession by my graphics teacher. He wanted me to document my fixation with drawing. I doodled on some furniture, clothes and my childhood bedroom.”
“I was fine with that,” Andrea interjects, as we step into the kitchen: doodled oven, doodled taster, doodled extractor fan. “He also asked to do the family bathroom. That was a no.”
“The obvious next step was a whole house,” Sam says. “It was always a target in my head.”
In December 2019, the purchase complete, Sam’s uncle Graham Wells – a builder – was tasked with stripping the house back to its bones. Every surface, inside and out, was painted white – a nearly 5,000 sq ft blank canvas. It took a little over two years, all in, for Sam to decorate the house in its entirety: spray paint on the outside, black acrylic and bingo markers indoors. The result is a truly transfixing optical overload.
View image in fullscreen
‘A whole house was always a target in my head’: Cox’s home.
Photograph: Julian Anderson/The Guardian
We all settle on the doodled sofas. His parents’ house – where Sam was raised – is a short walk through the village. “I tried to talk him out of it at first,” Andrea says, sipping from her doodled teacup. “We looked around with the last owners who asked if Sam was going to doodle it. No, he told them. I’m not sure it would have been sold to him if they’d known. For the exterior, I came up with all sorts of alternative suggestions. Why not try projections? Then you could switch it off.” Sam was having none of it. “We’ve had no complaints from the neighbours. I know it was your dream,” she glances over at her adult child, “but it was like being in a nightmare at the time.”
Sam, who is listening quietly, fidgets his fingers. To the millions of followers who watched online, the house’s transformation was a triumph. Set to jaunty music,
one time-lapse victory video
documenting his efforts has been watched some

data.title: Why is the Rust compiler so slow?
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust编译器在Docker中构建速度慢的问题，特别是在使用静态链接和部署网站时。每次修改代码后，完全重建需要约4分钟，主要瓶颈在于最终二进制文件的编译时间。文章介绍了一种利用`cargo-chef`工具实现依赖缓存的方法，以加快构建速度。然而，即使使用缓存，最终二进制文件的编译仍需约2分50秒。作者深入分析了Rust编译器（`rustc`）和LLVM的优化过程，试图找出进一步加速的方法。虽然尝试了一些优化，但效果有限，最终建议接受目前的速度，或考虑其他如增量编译等方法来改善开发体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust编译速度及其相关技术与社会因素

不同观点：
• saghm认为，Rust编译时间长的主要问题不是编译速度本身，而是难以避免编译大量不必要的依赖代码。他提出这是一个技术问题，与依赖过多的社会问题不同。
• taylorallred通过C语言中RAD调试器的快速编译例子，质疑为什么Rust和Swift无法实现类似的速度，暗示这些语言的编译速度可能有改进空间。
• dminik指出，Rust项目可能由于宏和泛型的大量使用，导致实际编译的代码量远超预期，尽管这些特性本身很有价值。同时提到async-graphql库的性能问题。
• rednafi对比Go语言，认为Go通过牺牲一些优化和类型系统的复杂性，实现了更快的编译速度，并认为这种权衡在某些开发场景中是合理的。
• ahartmetz对容器与单一静态二进制文件的管理复杂度提出质疑，暗示使用容器可能导致不必要的复杂性。
• MangoToupe认为Rust的编译速度与其他同类语言相比并不算慢，并指出相比C++和Scala的15分钟编译时间，Rust表现更好。
• kenoath69提到使用Cranelift显著改善了游戏开发中的编译时间问题，建议在相关讨论中提及Cranelift。
• adastra22作为前C++开发者，对Rust编译慢的说法感到不解。
• namibj建议使用增量编译并结合Docker缓存来优化编译过程，提出了一种具体的操作方法。
• Scuds分享了在M1 Pro上编译Deno项目的具体时间数据，指出未使用增量编译的情况下编译时间较长，但CI/CD系统可以解决这一问题。
• AndyKelley对比Zig语言的编译速度，展示其项目的快速编译时间，强调增量编译的有效性。
• edude03认为文章混淆了Docker环境下的构建慢与编译器本身的慢，并指出Rust增量编译在开发模式下速度是可以接受的。
• ozgrakkurt认为Rust编译慢是因为开发者过度使用泛型和宏，导致代码生成过多，并指出社区对编译速度的重视不够。
• duped指出很多人没有仔细阅读文章，误解了在Docker中构建Rust项目的具体方法，提供了更优化的构建建议。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种优化Rust编译速度的方法，包括增量编译、Cranelift的使用、Docker缓存管理等。
• 对比了Rust与其他语言（如Go、C、C++、Zig）的编译速度，提出了不同语言在编译速度与功能复杂性之间的权衡。
• 强调了社区和开发者习惯对编译速度的影响，提出了对滥用语言特性的批评。
• 具体技术建议包括使用增量编译、优化Docker构建过程、利用Cranelift等工具。

"Why is the Rust compiler so slow?"
26 Jun 2025 at 00:34:13 +01:00
I spent a month repeatedly building my website in Docker, and now have horrors to share.
I've got a problem.
My website (the one you're reading right now) is mainly served by a single Rust binary.
For
far too long
now, every time I wanted to make a change, I would:
Build a new statically linked binary (with
--target=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
)
Copy it to my server
Restart the website
This is... not ideal.
So instead, I'd like to switch to deploying my website with containers (be it Docker, Kubernetes, or otherwise),
matching the vast majority of software deployed any time in the last decade.
The only issue is that fast Rust builds with Docker are not simple.
Update (2025-06-27)
I first posted this
on Bluesky
— there was some
good discussion there
❤️
Special thanks to Piotr Osiewicz & Wesley Moore for suggestions that saved a ton more time.
More on those
closer to the end
.
It was also reposted over on
r/rust
,
r/programming
and
hackernews
. Plenty of entertaining comments, if you're in
the mood.
Table of Contents:
Basics: Rust in Docker
What's
rustc
doing for all that time?
Actually asking
rustc
this time
It's time to talk about LTO
A brief note: 50 seconds is
fine
, actually!
Another brief note: Can't we just use incremental compilation?
Digging deeper: Et tu,
LLVM_module_optimize
?
What's LLVM's deal?
What's in LLVM's trace events?
Can we make
InlinerPass
any faster?
Can we make
OptFunction
any faster?
Putting it together
Update 2025-06-27
Final recap
Basics: Rust in Docker
Rust in Docker, the simple way
To get your Rust program in a container, the typical approach you might find would be something
like:
FROM
rust:1.87-alpine3.22
AS
builder
RUN
apk add musl-dev
WORKDIR
/workdir
COPY
. .
# the "package" for my website is "web-http-server".
RUN
cargo build --package web-http-server --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
# Only include the binary in the final image
FROM
alpine:3.20
COPY
--from
=
builder
/workdir/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/web-http-server /usr/bin/web-http-server
ENTRYPOINT
[
"/usr/bin/web-http-server"
]
Unfortunately, this will rebuild everything from scratch whenever there's any change
.
In my case, building from scratch takes about 4 minutes (including 10s to download the crates every time).
$
cargo
build
--release
--target
=
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
--package
web-http-server
Updating crates.io index
Downloading crates ...
Downloaded anstream v0.6.18
Downloaded http-body v1.0.1
... many more lines ...
Compiling web-http-server v0.1.0 (/workdir/web-http-server)
Finished `release` profile [optimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 3m 51s
Sure, it could be worse. But I've grown accustomed to speedy local builds, thanks to incremental compilation — I don't
want to wait that long on every tiny change!
Rust in Docker, with better caching
Thankfully, there's a tool to help with this!
Luca Palmieri's
cargo-chef
makes it easy to pre-build all of the dependencies as a separate layer in the docker
build cache, so that changes in your codebase only trigger re-compilation of your codebase (and not your dependencies).
I'll save the detailed explanation for
Luca's blog post
, but broadly
cargo-chef
creates a simplified "recipe" file from
the current workspace, which can be "cooked" to cache the dependencies without being invalidated by changes in the
workspace.
My website pulls in a few hundred dependencies, so this
should
help!
...
FROM
...
AS
planner
COPY
. .
RUN
cargo chef prepare --recipe-path=/workdir/recipe.json
FROM
...
AS
cooker
# NOTE: changes to the project can produce the same "recipe",
# allowing this build stage to be cached.
COPY
--from
=
planner
/workdir/recipe.json recipe.json
RUN
cargo chef cook --release --recipe-path=/workdir/recipe.json
\
--target=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
# If recipe.json is the same, 'cooker' will be cached.
# All that's left is compiling the final binary.
FROM
cooker
AS
builder
COPY
. .
RUN
cargo build --release --package web-http-server
\
--target=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
Unfortunately though, it doesn't have quite the speedup we're looking for — most of the time is still in the final
binary:
$
# Build dependencies
$
cargo
chef cook
--release
..
.
Updating crates.io index
Downloading crates ...
...
Compiling web-http-server v0.0.1 (/workdir/web-http-server)
Finished `release` profile [optimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 07s
$
# Build the final binary, using cached dependencies
$
cargo
build
--release
..
.
Compiling web-http-server v0.1.0 (/workdir/web-http-server)
Finished `release` profile [optimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 50s
Weirdly, only 25% of the time is actually spent on the dependencies! As far as I could tell, my code isn't doing
anything fundamentally unreasonable. It's ~7k lines of gluing together various larger dependencies (
axum
,
reqwest
,
tokio-postgres
, among others.)

cargo build
with
--verbose
. It really was just a single
inv

data.title: Parameterized types in C using the new tag compatibility rule
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
C23引入了一种新的标签兼容性规则，允许在不同翻译单元中定义的具有相同标签和字段的结构体、联合体和枚举类型相互兼容。这一变化使得使用宏进行类型参数化成为可能。以前，每个翻译单元内的定义都是不同的类型，不兼容。现在可以定义类似如下的参数化宏：

```c
#define Slice(T) \
struct Slice##T { \
T *data; \
ptrdiff_t len; \
ptrdiff_t cap; \
}
```

这允许在需要时动态生成不同元素类型的切片，例如`Slice(int)`或`Slice(float)`。此外，结合C23的`typeof`关键字，可以实现更灵活的动态数组操作，例如通用的`push`宏。然而，这种方法仍有限制，不能用于定义如`Map(K, V)`这样的复杂结构，因为宏参数必须是标识符，且嵌套使用时较为不便。总体而言，这一新规则提供了一种有限的C++模板机制，但仅限于类型参数化，函数操作上仍缺乏泛型支持。

主要讨论点：C语言中宏和泛型的使用以及最近提案对C语言的影响

• 不同评论者对C语言的改进方向存在争议，主要集中在是否应引入类似C++的模板机制以及这些改进对代码可读性和类型安全的影响。
• 提案的具体实现细节和技术选择（如ptrdiff_t的使用）也引发了一些讨论。

C23 has
a new rule for struct, union, and enum compatibility
finally appearing in compilers starting with GCC 15, released this past
April, and Clang later this year. The same struct defined in different
translation units (TU) has always been compatible — essential to how they
work. Until this rule change, each such definition within a TU was a
distinct, incompatible type. The new rule says that,
ackshually
, they
are compatible! This unlocks some type parameterization using macros.
How can a TU have multiple definitions of a struct? Scope. Prior to C23
this wouldn’t compile because the compound literal type and the return
type were distinct types:
struct
Example
{
int
x
,
y
,
z
;
};
struct
Example
example
(
void
)
{
struct
Example
{
int
x
,
y
,
z
;
};
return
(
struct
Example
){
1
,
2
,
3
};
}
Otherwise the definition of
struct Example
within
example
was fine, if
strange. At first this may not seem like a big deal, but let’s
revisit my
technique for dynamic arrays
:
typedef
struct
{
T
*
data
;
ptrdiff_t
len
;
ptrdiff_t
cap
;
}
SliceT
;
Where I write out one of these for each
T
that I might want to put into
a slice. With the new rule we can change it slightly, taking note of the
introduction of a tag (the name after
struct
):
#define Slice(T)        \
struct Slice##T {   \
T        *data; \
ptrdiff_t len;  \
ptrdiff_t cap;  \
}
This makes the “write it out ahead of time” thing simpler, but with the
new rule we can skip the “ahead of time” part and conjure slice types on
demand. Each declaration with the same
T
is compatible with the others
due to matching tags and fields. So, for example, with this macro we can
declare functions using slices parameterized for different element types.

(
int
)
range
(
int
,

*
);

(

(
float
));

(

(

,
char

,

*
);

(
Slice
(
Str
),
char
delim
,

*
);
Or using it with
our model parser
:

I worried these macros might confuse my tools, particularly

Ctags
because
it’s important to me

prototypes better than expected, but ctags doesn’t see fields with slice
types. Overall they’re like a very limited form of C++ templates. Though
only the types are parameterized, not the functions operating on those
types. Outside of unwarranted macro abuse, this new technique does nothing
regarding generic functions. On the other hand, my generic slice function
complements the new technique, especially with the help of C23’s new
typeof
to mitigate
_Alignof

char
*
beg
,

;

((s)->len == (s)->cap                     \
? (s)->data = push_(                    \
(a),                                \
(s)->data,                          \

sizeof(*(s)->data),                 \

void
*

{

data.title: Glass nanostructures reflect nearly all visible light, challenging assumptions
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 新加坡科技设计大学（SUTD）的研究团队开发出一种新方法，通过3D打印纳米级玻璃结构，实现了接近100%的可见光反射率，颠覆了以往对低折射率材料在光子学中应用的认知。该团队使用了一种名为Glass-Nano的光敏树脂，通过双光子光刻技术打印出具有260纳米特征的结构，并在650°C的烧结过程中保持形状和精度。这种方法克服了传统硅基材料的颗粒感和低分辨率问题，成功制造出高均匀性的钻石型光子晶体，反射性能媲美高折射率材料。研究结果表明，通过精细的结构控制，低折射率材料也能在光子学领域表现出色，为可穿戴光学设备、集成显示器和传感器等应用开辟了新可能。

Nanoscale 3D printing of glass. Credit:
Science Advances
(2025). DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.adv0267
A research team led by SUTD has created nanoscale glass structures with near-perfect reflectance, overturning long-held assumptions about what low-index materials can do in photonics.
For decades, glass has been a reliable workhorse of optical systems, valued for its transparency and stability. But when it comes to manipulating light at the nanoscale, especially for high-performance optical devices, glass has traditionally taken a backseat to higher refractive index materials. Now, a research team led by Professor Joel Yang from the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) is reshaping this narrative.
With findings
published
in
Science Advances
, the team has developed a new method to 3D-print glass structures with nanoscale precision and achieve nearly 100% reflectance in the
visible spectrum
. This level of performance is rare for low-refractive-index materials like silica, and it opens up a broader role for glass in nanophotonics, including in wearable optics, integrated displays, and sensors.
The researchers' breakthrough is enabled by a new material called Glass-Nano: a photocurable resin made by blending silicon-containing molecules with other light-sensitive organic compounds.
Unlike conventional approaches that rely on silica nanoparticles—often resulting in grainy, low-resolution structures—Glass-Nano cures smoothly and contracts uniformly during heating, transforming into clear, robust glass. When printed using two-photon lithography, these polymer structures shrink during sintering at 650°C, preserving their form while achieving nanoscale features as small as 260 nanometers.
"Instead of starting with silica particles, we worked with silicon-bearing molecules in the resin formulation," explained Prof Yang. "This resin enables us to build up nanostructures with much finer detail and smoother surfaces than was previously possible. We then convert them into glass using our 'print-and-shrink' process without sacrificing fidelity."
The team focused their fabrication on photonic crystals (PhCs)—artificially structured materials featuring repeating patterns that interact with specific wavelengths of light. These structures can reflect light very efficiently, but only if built with extreme regularity and precision. Previous efforts to realize low-index 3D PhCs have consistently fallen short, exhibiting only poor reflectance due to structural irregularities and distortions.
With their new method, the researchers overcame these limitations. By printing more than 20 tightly stacked layers and fine-tuning the design geometry, they achieved a structurally highly uniform, diamond-like photonic crystal that reflects nearly 100% of incident light within a broad range of viewing angles.
"The result was unexpected," shared Dr. Wang Zhang, SUTD Research Fellow and first author of the paper. "Historically, low-index materials like silica were seen as optically weak for this purpose. But our findings show that with enough uniformity and structural control, they can outperform expectations—and even rival high-index materials in reflectance."

Preserving the structural shape during the dramatic shrinkage process was no small feat.
"At the macroscale, shrinkage like this would collapse the structure," Dr. Zhang added. "But at the nanoscale, the high surface-to-volume ratio actually helps preserve stability. 44365404.article_summary: 新加坡科技设计大学（SUTD）的研究团队开发出一种新方法，通过3D打印纳米级玻璃结构，实现了接近100%的可见光反射率，颠覆了以往对低折射率材料在光子学中应用的认知。该团队使用了一种名为Glass-Nano的光敏树脂，通过双光子光刻技术打印出具有260纳米特征的结构，并在650°C的烧结过程中保持形状和精度。这种方法克服了传统硅基材料的颗粒感和低分辨率问题，成功制造出高均匀性的钻石型光子晶体，反射性能媲美高折射率材料。研究结果表明，通过精细的结构控制，低折射率材料也能在光子学领域表现出色，为可穿戴光学设备、集成显示器和传感器等应用开辟了新可能。

data.title: Tennis Scorigami
data.author: jlarks32
data.article_summary: 自1968年以来的57年间，尽管进行了大量网球比赛，但仍有一些比分组合从未出现过。这个项目旨在追踪和发现这些缺失的比分线。在所有可能的比分中，只有一部分曾在比赛中出现，其余的则尚未发生。项目提供互动方式，供用户探索哪些具体比分组合至今未在比赛中出现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对网站内容、功能及用户体验的不同看法

不同观点：
• [pimlottc] 认为自动轮播更新的比分框令人困扰，特别是在移动端下滑后无法轻易停止轮播，这影响了用户体验。他指出虽然可以手动停止轮播，但这一点并不明显。

• [npinsker] 对足球比赛中的"Scorigami"（稀有比分）现象表示欣赏，认为不同寻常的比分背后有故事和历史，能让人从不同角度欣赏足球。不过，他表示对网站上的具体数字并不感兴趣，但称赞了网站的设计美观。

• [jedberg] 关注比分缺失的现象，指出一些不常见的比分组合（如6-0和0-6）很少出现，并解释这种不平衡比分在比赛中极少发生，因此在统计中缺失是合理的。

• [ben0x539] 被网站上可爱的鼠标互动设计吸引，尚未深入了解网站内容，表明网站的某些设计元素（如鼠标互动）可能分散了用户对主要内容的注意力。

• [yzyzserd] 总结了在女子三盘两胜和男子五盘三胜比赛中的未出现比分情况，并指出在大量可能性中，只有少数比分组合在实际比赛中发生过。此外，他还对复杂的用户界面（UI）提出了批评。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于自动轮播功能对用户体验的影响，部分用户认为其不便且不明显。
- 用户对网站内容的兴趣点不同，有的关注比分及其背后的故事，有的则更在意设计元素。
- 比分缺失现象引起了对比赛统计数据和实际比赛情况的讨论，部分用户尝试解释这种现象的合理性。
- 用户界面（UI）的复杂性也是讨论的一个方面，有用户认为其过于繁琐。

data.title: Infrastructure at Roblox
data.author: ak009
data.article_summary: Roblox通过创新工程方法和基础设施支持数千万用户同时在线游玩，包括处理如《Grow a Garden》打破吉尼斯世界纪录时的流量激增。Roblox在全球管理24个边缘数据中心和2个核心数据中心，通过私有全球网络互连，以最小化延迟并保护核心服务。为应对流量波动，Roblox提前两年预测容量需求，并通过每周的规划、测试和调整来确保平台稳定。工程团队通过主动学习和敏捷周期，快速适应如《Dress to Impress》和《Dead Rails》等游戏的突然流行，确保创作者无需担心容量问题，同时保持新功能持续发布。Roblox的基础设施创新基于四大核心价值，包括长远视角和尊重社区，以支持平台不断打破并发用户记录。

主要讨论点：Roblox的技术架构、安全性、商业模式以及对儿童的影响

不同观点：

• **对平台兼容性的不满（greatgib）**：由于Roblox不支持Linux客户端，用户不得不选择其他游戏平台（如Minecraft）来满足需求。

• **对商业模式的批评（kgwxd）**：认为Roblox的商业模式是针对儿童生日钱的骗局，暗示其微交易机制对儿童和家长不公平。

• **反对儿童玩Roblox的观点（notnmeyer）**：认为Roblox含有不当和未被审核的内容，且过度强调微交易，不适合儿童单独玩耍。

• **对技术选择的幽默评论（purpleidea）**：以半开玩笑的方式指出，如果Roblox不使用Kubernetes，可能只需要现有容量的10%，暗示当前架构可能存在过度设计。

• **争议焦点**：Roblox的商业模式和其对儿童的影响是主要争议点。支持者认为其对儿童有教育意义且环境安全，而反对者则认为其含有不当内容且过度依赖微交易。

The Infrastructure Supporting Record-Breaking Experiences
Reaching New Heights Every Weekend on Roblox
By
Anupam Singh, Senior Vice President of Engineering
Published
Jun 24, 2025
Robloxâs ability to scale and support tens of millions of users playing together across millions of unique experiences isnât the result of a single innovation. Itâs the sum of a broader culture of innovation and a thousand small things done well across the company. This is how weâve built the infrastructure thatâs currently supporting record-breaking traffic to many of the experiences on Roblox. One of those experiences,
Grow a Garden
, recently broke the
Guinness World RecordsÂ®
achievement for most concurrently played video game, with 21.6 million users playing simultaneously. And in the process, the Roblox platform has continued to hit new peak concurrency records (as it has over nearly two decades), most recently exceeding 30 million concurrent players.
Roblox faces unique challenges in building and maintaining infrastructure for millions of creator-built experiences, including
Dress to Impress
,
Adopt Me
, and
Dead Rails
, requiring innovative engineering methodologies. The platform supports dozens of hourly updates and more than 30 million concurrent users with infrastructure that scales during unexpected traffic spikes. This infrastructure must support thundering herd situations where more than 21 million users join a single experience simultaneously (and the update code came from independent creators). Roblox engineers innovate solutions by challenging traditional wisdomâsolutions that are inspired by our four core values.
Infrastructure at Roblox
Roblox engineers manage 24 edge data centers around the world, which run the game servers. When a user joins an experience, theyâre matched to the nearest data center and the most appropriate instance within the center to minimize latency. We also manage two core data centers, which are much larger and run centralized services like the website, recommendation algorithms, safety filters, virtual economy, and publishing platform, which are necessary for the edge data centers to function. A global private network interconnects all the edge data centers to the core data centers, with edge data centers serving as a firewall to protect services running in the core data center.
Take the Long View: Proactive Capacity Prediction
In an ideal world, our creators should never have to think about capacityâthe infrastructure should be invisible to them, working behind the scenes. When a creator publishes an experience to Roblox, our work is to support the capacity needed, no matter how many players show up. In the early days, we planned capacity once a year for the year or two ahead. But in recent years, successful experiences like
Dress to Impress
,
Fisch
,
Dead Rails
, and
Grow a Garden
have led us to rethink our framework for capacity planning.
In line with our value of taking the long view, we now predict capacity needs up to two years in advance, balancing user demand with efficient server utilization. Our planning cycle involves data center acquisition, server hardware refreshes, and physical networking, with new data centers like the one in Brazil being planned years ahead. The networking team also maintains âdarkâ capacity to ensure continuous operation despite issues like network cable cuts.
The capacity Roblox has today is based on predictions made two years ago, when we couldnât have predicted experiences growing from unknown to huge popularity within weeks. Popular games like Dress to Impress and Grow a Garden, which helped double Roblox's peak concurrent player count from 13.9 million in April to 30.6 million in June 2025, didn't exist when these capacity predictions were made. For example, in March 2025, Dead Rails spiked to 1 million concurrent users, using all available CPU capacity.
Learning from these types of popularity spikes, weâve moved to a more agile planning cycle. To consistently support record player counts on Roblox, engineering employs a rigorous weekly cycle of planning, testing, and capacity adjustments. Monday is dedicated to incident reviews, followed by capacity planning on Tuesday. Throughout the week, thereâs continual chaos testing. Thursday focuses on reviewing capacity for any large updates our creators have told us to expect. On Friday, additional cloud resources are provisioned to ensure that the platform is prepared for peak weekend usage. Throughout the week, we continue to release entirely new features, and we do not lock the continuous deployment by all engineers.
Respect the Community: Effortless Capacity for Creators

data.title: Techie went home rather than fix mistake that caused a meltdown
data.author: docmechanic
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了IT经理Stuart在一家初创公司工作时，设计了一个用于监控实验室冷冻柜状态的系统。一次，他不小心将温度单位从摄氏度调成了华氏度，导致警报大作。他认为问题不严重，决定周一再修复，并关闭了警报系统。周末，一名电气承包商错误地切断了整栋建筑的电源，但未告知任何人。由于合同规定电力冗余，冷冻柜样本未受影响。周一，Stuart发现承包商的错误掩盖了他自己的失误，避免了责备。最终，Stuart的错误未造成实际损失。

On-Prem
154
Techie went home rather than fix mistake that caused a massive meltdown
154
And was saved by an even worse meltdown caused by someone else
Simon Sharwood
Mon 23 Jun 2025
//
07:26 UTC
Who, Me?
Welcome to another working week and therefore another installment of Who, Me? –
The Register
's reader-contributed column where you confess to making a mess and somehow find safe egress.
This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Stuart" who hoped his career would see him pursue pure research but found himself working as IT manager for what he described as "a very young startup spun out of a local research center to commercialize a novel gene analysis technique."
The IT team was small – Stuart plus a couple of contractors – but that meant our hero had "very nearly free rein in designing the systems, so the job was anything but boring."
He duly made security keys mandatory for authentication, implemented "paranoia-grade network partitioning" – native IPv6-only, naturally – and created an encrypted, append-only off-site data archive.
"You name it, if I could show it made sense I got to implement it," Stuart told Who, Me?
Stuart spotted one project that made a lot of sense. The startup kept a lot of samples in freezers and was contractually obliged to keep them safe for years. Creating a system to monitor that the freezers were in working order was an obvious win.
Lab-grade freezers are built to make this sort of project doable because they include sensors galore, employ the Modbus serial communication protocol, and can even pack an RS485 serial port to help the machines share sensor info with the world.
Stuart therefore pulled some extra wiring through the cabling ducts, configured a Raspberry Pi 1B to ingest data, and wrote Python scripts to feed info into the startup's monitoring infrastructure.
The resulting system was very simple. If a freezer door was left open too long, alerts went off.
"It proved hugely successful and popular among the lab techies because it was all too easy to leave those doors ajar, so we set out to extend the scope," Stuart wrote.
"It was only then that I realized that the specs provided by the freezer manufacturer were not in total agreement with reality on the freezers we had," he added.
Stuart tried to make sense of it all. One Friday, he accidentally tweaked a setting so the freezers monitored temperatures measured in Fahrenheit instead of Celsius – but didn't change alarm thresholds accordingly.
That has obvious potential for mayhem given that 32° Fahrenheit is 0° Celsius.
Within seconds of unwittingly making this mistake, alerts flashed across Stuart's freezer-monitoring dashboards.
He had no idea of the cause, but as the freezer doors were closed, he didn't think it was important enough to warrant an immediate fix.
Techie exposed giant tax grab, maybe made government change the rules
Field support chap got married – which took down a mainframe
Admin brought his drill to work, destroyed disks and crashed a datacenter
Techies thought outside the box. Then the boss decided to take the box away
Then another emergency erupted and consumed the rest of the Friday. Stuart figured he could fix the freezer monitor on Monday, so he turned off his alarms and went home for the weekend.
The next day, an electrical contractor made a worse mistake.
"He managed to somehow trip every single circuit breaker in the building and left without saying a word to anyone," Stuart told Who, Me?
The problem went unnoticed until Monday morning, when Stuart arrived at work and was relieved to find nobody blamed him for the mess.
"Our lease specified redundant power for the freezers and required that weekend electrical work be announced well in advance," he told Who, Me?
Recriminations therefore focused on the landlord, not Stuart's tech.
This story has a happy ending because, despite the meltdown, the samples in the freezers survived intact.
"Even so, my very first thought after coming to work on that day and learning what had happened was 'Oh, BUGGER,'" Stuart told Who, Me?
Has someone else's mistake saved you from being blamed for your own errors? If so,

44410159.article_summary: 本文讲述了IT经理Stuart在一家初创公司工作时，设计了一个用于监控实验室冷冻柜状态的系统。一次，他不小心将温度单位从摄氏度调成了华氏度，导致警报大作。他认为问题不严重，决定周一再修复，并关闭了警报系统。周末，一名电气承包商错误地切断了整栋建筑的电源，但未告知任何人。由于合同规定电力冗余，冷冻柜样本未受影响。周一，Stuart发现承包商的错误掩盖了他自己的失误，避免了责备。最终，Stuart的错误未造成实际损失。

data.title: Universal pre-training by iterated random computation
data.author: liamdgray
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了利用随机生成数据进行模型预训练的方法。基于算法复杂性理论，作者证明了这种方法的合理性，并通过实验表明，合成数据预训练的模型能够在多种数据集上实现零样本上下文学习，且性能随模型规模提升而增强。此外，作者还将结果扩展到真实数据，显示预训练后微调的模型具有更快的收敛速度和更好的泛化能力。研究结果支持随机计算预训练在提升模型性能方面的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用合成数据进行预训练模型的效果及实验设计

不同观点：
• **Visarga**：认为实验结果一般，仅减少了20-30%的训练步骤，无法解决数据匮乏的问题。他指出，实验仅对比了随机初始化模型和使用合成数据的预训练模型（A vs C），而没有对比使用自然语言语料预训练的模型（B）和合成数据预训练模型（A）的效果，质疑实验的全面性。Visarga强调需要更多真实数据（100x）来真正解决问题。

• **Bionhoward**：对该方法表示兴趣，但认为实验缺乏一个不使用通用预训练数据的对照组。他建议增加一个完全不使用预训练数据的控制组，以便更好地展示预训练的效果。此外，他提议比较使用随机数据的模型与未使用随机数据的模型在后期评估数据上的学习能力，并建议通过比较预训练前后的模型检查点来验证方法的有效性。Bionhoward承认自己只是略读了论文，但认为增加这些控制会更有说服力。

• **Liamdgray**：引用了论文摘要，强调了研究从算法复杂性的理论角度支持使用随机生成数据进行预训练，并展示了合成数据预训练的模型在多种数据集上表现出零样本上下文学习的能力。他指出，实验结果表明预训练后进行微调可以带来更快的收敛速度和更好的泛化能力。

补充讨论：
• 实验设计的全面性是争议焦点，Visarga和Bionhoward都指出了对照实验的不足，特别是缺乏与自然语言语料预训练模型的直接对比（A vs B）。
• Visarga对合成数据能否替代真实数据持怀疑态度，认为需要更多真实数据来验证方法的有效性，而Liamdgray则更关注该方法在理论和实验上的潜力。
• Bionhoward对实验持开放态度，但希望通过增加控制实验来进一步验证研究结论的可靠性。

44409555.article_content:
Computer Science > Machine Learning
arXiv:2506.20057
(cs)
[Submitted on 24 Jun 2025]
Title:
Universal pre-training by iterated random computation
Authors:
Peter Bloem
View a PDF of the paper titled Universal pre-training by iterated random computation, by Peter Bloem
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We investigate the use of randomly generated data for the sake of pre-training a model. We justify this approach theoretically from the perspective of algorithmic complexity, building on recent research that shows that sequence models can be trained to approximate Solomonoff induction. We derive similar, but complementary theoretical results. We show empirically that synthetically generated data can be used to pre-train a model before the data is seen. We replicate earlier results that models trained this way show zero-shot in-context learning across a variety of datasets, and that this performance improves with scale. We extend earlier results to real-world data, and show that finetuning a model after pre-training offers faster convergence and better generalization.

data.title: Generative AI's crippling failure to induce robust models of the world
data.author: pmcjones
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）是否能建立对世界的理解，以及其局限性和潜力。

不同观点：
• tim333认为，虽然LLMs目前仅能模拟语言，但未来可能具备对世界更深入的理解，包括空间、时间、情感等概念。他认为LLMs目前缺乏人类对世界的理解，但未来AI有可能克服这一局限。
• SubiculumCode支持AI发展进入“AI冬季”，认为当前社会无法快速适应AI带来的变化。当前AI水平能提高生产力，但不会让人类变得无关紧要。
• extr认为Garry Marcus的论点过于语义化且缺乏说服力，指出Marcus没有明确的世界模型定义和评估基准，并质疑其观点的实际意义。extr同时表示，尽管LLMs可能没有世界模型，但它们仍然具有实用价值。
• energy123质疑为何未讨论Anthropic的可解释性工作，暗示这可能对结论不利。
• Animats将LLMs缺乏世界模型的问题与工程师和经理之间的沟通问题类比，指出经理可能缺乏任务的心理模型但仍试图指导。
• vunderba通过实验指出，当前VLM在识别棋盘上棋子数量时在不可能的局面下有更高错误率，说明其局限性。
• sdenton4讨论了死reckoning导航方式的局限性，并指出蚂蚁通过信息素和嗅觉找到回家的路，而非符号化的GOFAI方式。
• Animats认为LLMs的黑箱性质和缺乏世界模型是两个独立的问题，指出有些黑箱系统确实有底层模型，并提到早期机器学习方法的白箱性质。
• voidhorse认为LLMs只是优秀的词预测器，任何认为它们在思考的观点都是极端拟人化的营销说辞。他质疑是否通过预测词就能产生推理能力，并用潜艇不被称为游泳的例子类比。
• dist-epoch提到一个实验，通过LLM解密受限内容，显示其未拒绝提供危险信息，暗示LLMs在安全性上的问题。
• UltraSane引用一篇论文，主张世界模型是灵活、目标导向行为的重要组成部分，并提供形式化的证明，认为提高 agent 的性能或复杂性需要学习更精确的世界模型。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到LLMs的黑箱性质、世界模型的定义和评估基准问题。
• 有对LLMs当前实用价值的认可，但对其未来发展方向和潜在风险存在争议。
• 提到了Anthropic的可解释性工作和LLMs在安全性上的问题，显示出对LLMs伦理和安全性的关注。
• 不同论据涉及到生物学和工程学的类比，显示跨学科的讨论。

data.title: Blackwell: Nvidia's GPU
data.author: pella
data.article_summary:
Nvidia的Blackwell架构延续了其制造大型GPU的传统，其中GB202是最大芯片，面积达750mm2，拥有922亿个晶体管和192个流式多处理器（SMs）。GB202用于RTX PRO 6000，是Nvidia目前最高配置的GPU，而RTX 5090则在部分SMs上做了屏蔽。相比之下，AMD的RDNA4系列顶级产品为RX 9070和9070XT，后者在32个WGPs中屏蔽了4个。

Blackwell的SM与图形处理集群（GPC）比例为1:16，相比Ada Lovelace的1:12，能在不增加GPC硬件的情况下提升计算吞吐量。不过，短期波形任务可能难以充分利用Blackwell的规模，因GPC分配工作的速度可能成为瓶颈。

此外，Blackwell改进了工作负载调度，取消了子通道切换，允许不同类型任务在同一队列中更高效地混合执行。SM前端采用128位固定长度指令和两级指令缓存设计，以应对高带宽需求并保持性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NVIDIA与AMD的GPU对比及其在不同应用场景（如计算、游戏、AI）中的适用性，以及对NVIDIA未来发展的猜测。

不同观点：
• **ggreg84**：认为Chips and Cheese对GPU的OpenCL分析非常详细，但这些结果仅适用于OpenCL，而大多数使用NVIDIA或AMD GPU进行计算的用户使用的是CUDA或HIP。这些技术在编译堆栈上有很大差异，因此OpenCL的分析结果不能直接应用于CUDA，质疑其分析的实际应用价值。

• **Aissen**：指出评论中对比的AMD桌面GPU与NVIDIA工作站加速器之间有巨大的价格差异（相差一个数量级），质疑这种对比是否有意义。

• **CalChris**：提供了一个技术细节，引用了Nvidia的技术简报，指出Nvidia某款GPU拥有2080亿个晶体管，并使用TSMC 4NP工艺。他进行了粗略估算，展示了每个晶体管的面积，同时指出工艺特征尺寸与实际晶体管尺寸的不同。

• **ksec**：提到目前购买消费级Nvidia GPU仍有困难，讨论了可能的原因（游戏市场需求、AI需求或供应链问题）。同时，期待Nvidia进入CPU市场，并预测未来CPU的重要性可能下降，Nvidia可能将CPU作为系统中的附加组件推出，特别是考虑到ARM X930有可能在IPC上与Apple M4竞争。

• **dist-epoch**：质疑为什么NVIDIA不开发像Google TPU那样的处理器（如 systolic array），这种处理器虽然可编程性较低，但在吞吐量和能效上更具优势。特别指出推理市场有巨大的需求。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：ggreg84对Chips and Cheese的分析结果是否适用于CUDA提出了质疑，而Aissen则质疑AMD和NVIDIA产品之间的价格和应用场景差异是否使得对比失去意义。
• **对未来的预测**：ksec和dist-epoch对NVIDIA未来发展方向提出了不同看法，ksec期待NVIDIA进入CPU市场，而dist-epoch则希望NVIDIA开发更高效的处理器如TPU。

Nvidia has a long tradition of building giant GPUs. Blackwell, their latest graphics architecture, continues that tradition. GB202 is the largest Blackwell die. It occupies a massive 750mm2 of area, and has 92.2 billion transistors. GB202 has 192 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), the closest equivalent to a CPU core on a GPU, and feeds them with a massive memory subsystem. Nvidia’s RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell features the largest GB202 configuration to date. It sits alongside the RTX 5090 in Nvidia’s lineup, which also uses GB202 but disables a few more SMs.
A high level comparison shows the scale of Nvidia’s largest Blackwell products. AMD’s RDNA4 line tops out with the RX 9070 and RX 9070XT. The RX 9070 is slightly cut down, with four WGPs disabled out of 32. I’ll be using the RX 9070 to provide comparison data.
Acknowledgement
A massive thanks to Will Killian for giving us access to his RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell system for us to test. And so, a massive thanks goes out to him for this article!
Work Distribution
GPUs use specialized hardware to launch threads across their cores, unlike CPUs that rely on software scheduling in the operating system. Hardware thread launch is well suited to the short and simple tasks that often characterize GPU workloads. Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) are the basic building block of Nvidia GPUs, and are roughly analogous to a CPU core. SMs are grouped into Graphics Processing Clusters (GPCs), which contain a rasterizer and associated work distribution hardware.
GB202 has a 1:16 SM to GPC ratio, compared to the 1:12 ratio found in Ada Lovelace’s largest AD102 die. That lets Nvidia cheaply increase SM count and thus compute throughput without needing more copies of GPC-level hardware. However, dispatches with short-duration waves may struggle to take advantage of Blackwell’s scale, as throughput becomes limited by how fast the GPC can allocate work to the SMs rather than how fast the SMs can finish them.
AMD’s RDNA4 uses a 1:8 SE:WGP ratio, so one rasterizer feeds a set of eight WGPs in a Shader Engine. WGPs on AMD are the closest equivalent to SMs on Nvidia, and have the same nominal vector lane count. RDNA4 will be easier to utilize with small dispatches and short duration waves, but it’s worth noting that Blackwell’s design is not out of the ordinary. Scaling up GPU “cores” independently of work distribution hardware is a common technique for building larger GPUs. AMD’s RX 6900XT (RDNA2) had a 1:10 SE:WGP ratio. Before that, AMD’s largest GCN implementations like Fury X and Vega 64 had a 1:16 SE:CU ratio (CUs, or Compute Units, formed the basic building block of GCN GPUs). While Blackwell does have the same ratio as those large GCN parts, it enjoys higher clock speeds and likely has a higher wave launch rate to match per-GPU-core throughput. It won’t suffer as much as the Fury X from 10 years ago with short duration waves, but GB202 will still be harder to feed than smaller GPUs.
Example from RDNA2 with pixel shader (blue) and compute (yellow) work overlapping. Blackwell is now capable of this
Although Nvidia didn’t scale up work distribution hardware, they did make improvements on Blackwell. Prior Nvidia generations could not overlap workloads of different types on the same queue. Going between graphics and compute tasks would require a “subchannel switch” and a “wait-for-idle”. That requires one task on the queue to completely finish before the next can start, even if a game doesn’t ask for synchronization. Likely, higher level scheduling hardware that manages queues exposed to host-side applications can only track state for one workload type at a time. Blackwell does away with subchannel switches, letting it more efficiently fill its shader array if applications frequently mix different work types on the same queue.
SM Frontend
Once assigned work, the SM’s frontend fetches shader program instructions and delivers them to the execution units. Blackwell uses fixed length 128-bit (16 byte) instructions, and the SM uses a two-level instruction caching setup. Both characteristics are carried forward from Nvidia’s post-Turing/Volta designs. Each of the SM’s four partitions has a private L0 instruction cache, while a L1 instruction cache is shared across the SM.
Nvidia’s long 16 byte instructions translate to high instruction-side bandwidth demands. The L0+L1 instruction caching setup is likely intended to handle those bandwidth demands while also maintaining performance with larger code footprints. Each L0 only needs to provide one instruction per cycle, and its smaller size should make it easier to optimize for high bandwidth and low power. The SM-level L1 can then be optimized for capacity.

44409391.article_summary:
Nvidia的Blackwell架构延续了其制造大型GPU的传统，其中GB202是最大芯片，面积达750mm2，拥有922亿个晶体管和192个流式多处理器（SMs）。GB202用于RTX PRO 6000，是Nvidia目前最高配置的GPU，而RTX 5090则在部分SMs上做了屏蔽。相比之下，AMD的RDNA4系列顶级产品为RX 9070和9070XT，后者在32个WGPs中屏蔽了4个。

Blackwell的SM与图形处理集群（GPC）比例为1:16，相比Ada Lovelace的1:12，能在不增加GPC硬件的情况下提升计算吞吐量。不过，短期波形任务可能难以充分利用Blackwell的规模，因GPC分配工作的速度可能成为瓶颈。

此外，Blackwell改进了工作负载调度，取消了子通道切换，允许不同类型任务在同一队列中更高效地混合执行。SM前端采用128位固定长度指令和两级指令缓存设计，以应对高带宽需求并保持性能。

data.title: Group of investors represented by YouTuber Perifractic buys Commodore
data.author: erickhill
data.article_summary: 2025年6月28日，由Youtuber Perifractic（本名Christian Simpson）代表的一群投资者收购了拥有Commodore商标权的公司Commodore B.V.。收购以七位数的低价完成，但款项尚未付清，公司仍在寻找更多投资者。Perifractic成为临时CEO，并计划推出“复古未来主义”产品，旨在重现计算机技术被视为乌托邦的时代，尤其是 millennium 年间。他还提到Linux发行版Commodore OS Vision，并暗示下一个视频将揭晓具体产品。目前，公司正在招聘社交媒体经理和商品设计师。需要注意的是，Amiga品牌及相关软件的权利不属于此次收购的范围。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Commodore 品牌的重生及其相关产品和营销策略

不同观点：
• [0xbadc0de5] 认为，尽管支持该团队的努力和热情，但他们过早地发布了消息，且尚未实际支付品牌收购费用，这种冒险行为可能会导致计划失败，并吸引其他对品牌遗产不太真诚的 parties 注意。

• [card_zero] 建议新 CEO 立刻将 Commodore 品牌再次出售，将所得的 "七位数低端资金" 投资于新技术，成立一家名为 Rear Admiral 的新公司。

• [palmfacehn] 对实际产品是什么感到困惑，表示不想深入研究一系列视频，只是想要一个简洁的解释。

• [kragen] 指出，虽然新产品宣布出来了，但它并不是 Amiga 电脑，且 Amiga 品牌由 Gateway 2000 拥有。对 Commodore 陷入复古计算的泥潭表示遗憾。

• [andrewstuart] 对第一个发布的产品不是复古电脑而是某种反社交媒体产品感到奇怪，认为错失了让 C64 复活的真正机会，且反社交媒体与复古计算和 Commodore 毫无关联。

• [throwpoaster] 反对将计算机技术描述为 "人类的祸害"，认为这是对一个受人喜爱的品牌的糟糕宣传。

• [ChrisArchitect] 提到之前有 YouTuber 声称收到购买 Commodore 品牌的报价，提供了相关背景链接。

• [Theodores] 认为有时必须放手，执着于过去在科技行业没有意义。批评让今天的孩子学习过时的技术（如 BASIC 语言或滑尺）是不合适的，表示如果自己有资金和社交媒体影响力，会选择让孩子们学习更现代的技术。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于 Commodore 品牌的未来方向：一方认为应专注于复古计算和经典产品的复兴，另一方则认为应着眼于新技术和现代需求。
- 对品牌营销策略的质疑，包括过早宣布消息的风险，以及新产品方向是否符合品牌历史和受众期待。

28.Jun.2025
(ANF)
Group of investors represented by Youtuber Perifractic buys Commodore
Three weeks ago, Youtuber Christian 'Perifractic' Simpson
announced in a video
that he had received an offer to take over Commodore B.V., the owner of the remaining Commodore trademark rights. In a
second video
published today he now announces the completed takeover: A group of unnamed
angel investors
has acquired the company for a low seven-figure sum. He himself is now the acting CEO, but the purchase price has not yet been paid - the company is still looking for investors.
In the half-hour video, Simpson lists a whole series of former Commodore employees (Michael Tomczyk, Bil Herd, David Pleasance, support staff such as James Harrison and Hans Olsen) or actor Thomas Middleditch ("Silicon Valley") as future "advisors". A financial participation of the community is not yet possible, as the international legal hurdles are too high. Commodore plans to revive the time before social networks and artificial intelligence, when
computer technology was still considered a utopia rather than the scourge of mankind, with new "retro-futuristic" products. The years around the turn of the millennium are cited as a model several times.
There already seems to be a pretty clear idea of what Commodore's first "retro-futuristic" product will be - but Simpson won't reveal exactly what it is until the next video. Once again, however, the Youtuber praises the Linux distribution
Commodore OS Vision
, which was created during the Commodore USA era by former Commodore USA and future Commodore CTO Leo Nigro. This time it is explicitly described as "retro-futuristic", analogous to the planned hardware product.
In addition to further investors, in order to actually be able to pay the sum called for the sale, the company is currently looking for a social media manager and "merchandise designers".
Editor's note:
The Dutch company Commodore B.V., which Simpson and his investors have acquired, owns the "Commodore" trade marks and the "Chickenlips" logo. The rights to the Amiga brands and all 8-bit and Amiga software went to Gateway after the ESCOM bankruptcy and are now owned by Michael Battilana's Amiga Corp

data.title: Schizophrenia Is the Price We Pay for Minds Poised Near the Edge of a Cliff
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了精神分裂症在进化中的持久性问题。尽管精神分裂症是一种降低生育可能性的残疾精神疾病，但其终生患病率仍约为全球人口的1%。传统进化假说无法充分解释这一点。文章引用了Randolph Nesse的“悬崖边缘适应功能”假说，以及2024年Mitteroecker和Merola的论文，提出精神分裂症可能与某些认知、语言或社交特质的过度表达有关。这些特质在达到临界点前能提高适应性，但一旦超过该点，则会导致灾难性后果。自然选择使这些特质稳定在悬崖边缘之下，但少数个体可能越过临界点，导致适应性急剧下降。这种模型将精神分裂症视为进化过程中“悬崖边缘”现象的结果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于精神分裂症及其相关因素的多角度讨论，包括病因、治疗、基因以及环境影响等。

不同观点：
• suzzer99认为，她的朋友可能因长期使用迷幻药（如LSD和蘑菇）导致了精神病或精神分裂症的症状，并强调了这些药物的潜在风险。她引用了朋友在更年期后症状加剧的情况，怀疑荷尔蒙变化可能是一个诱因。

• bettercallsalad分享了与有精神病史的伴侣相处的个人经历，描述了伴侣在90%的时间里表现正常，但有时会出现严重的症状，如失眠、妄想和偏执。他也提到了药物治疗的有效性问题和对未来的不确定性。

• Throwaway42754自述患有由大麻引发的精神分裂情感障碍，强调了当前治疗方法的局限性和副作用，并表达了对新药物的期待。他还提到了生育问题，并支持使用胚胎筛查服务。

• drgo提出了一个假设，即精神分裂症相关基因可能在其他方面提供好处，如降低癌症风险，并引用了相关研究支持这一观点。

• boston_clone推荐了一篇研究论文，该论文对“悬崖边缘假说”进行了自我修正，并探讨了其他模糊因素。

• JamesBarney质疑了关于精神分裂症风险基因可能提高认知能力的观点，认为缺乏大规模的数据支持，并提出了现代环境可能更易触发精神分裂症的假设。

• discountdynamite介绍了Kasimir Dabrowski的“积极解体理论”，解释了人格发展中的过度兴奋和失败重组可能导致精神分裂症的机制。

• boardwaalk提到了“混沌边缘”理论，认为这一概念可能与精神分裂症等系统优化接近临界点的情况相关。

• sakoht提出了一个复杂的基因模型，认为多个基因的变异组合可能导致精神分裂症，并强调了相关基因在其他遗传背景下可能具有的益处。

• jonahbard讨论了自闭症与高智商之间的相关性，并提出了一个假设，即高智商/创造力/量化能力相关的基因可能无意中抑制了社交能力。

• subpixel分享了一个家庭成员患有精神分裂症的案例，强调了该病症可能伴随的高度智力和说服力，并指出了其对社会关系的破坏性影响。

• daft_pink好奇如何模型化近年来流行的减少繁殖行为，如在韩国养宠物而非生育孩子，以及这些行为在多代之后是否会被文化淘汰。

• cjbgkagh提出了RCCX基因簇与天赋之间的联系，并讨论了自身免疫和自律神经障碍在精神分裂症中的潜在作用。

• alganet分享了个人经历，描述了在36岁确诊后突然在音乐学习上表现出色，但对人际关系处理能力下降。他怀疑这些变化更多是心理性的而非基因相关，并对精神分裂症的典型触发因素持怀疑态度。

• voidhorse描述了个人经历中的“火脑”体验，强调了孤立和过度阅读可能导致的自由联想能力爆发，并提出了自己可能曾经处于精神分裂症的边缘。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了精神分裂症的多种潜在诱因，包括药物使用、遗传因素、荷尔蒙变化和现代环境影响等。
• 多种理论和假说被提出和讨论，如“悬崖边缘假说”、“混沌边缘”理论和“积极解体理论”，展示了精神分裂症复杂性和多样性的研究视角。

Schizophrenia Is the Price We Pay for Minds Poised Near the Edge of a Cliff
Cliff-edged fitness functions and the evolution of schizophrenia
Awais Aftab

This post discusses
cliff-edged fitness functions
by Randolph Nesse (psychiatrist and one of the founders of evolutionary medicine) and the 2024 paper, “
The cliff edge model of the evolution of schizophrenia: Mathematical, epidemiological, and genetic evidence,
” by Philipp Mitteroecker and Giuseppe Pierpaolo Merola.
If you are a regular reader of this newsletter, and it deepens your intellectual life,
consider a paid subscription
to support this effort.
The persistence of schizophrenia is an evolutionary enigma. It is a disabling psychiatric condition that reduces the likelihood of having children, and yet it has roughly 1% lifetime prevalence worldwide. Traditional evolutionary hypotheses, such as those invoking kin selection, mutation-selection balance, and evolutionary mismatch don’t quite explain this.
For instance, if schizophrenia risk genes were
not
under positive selection, we would expect them to be purged from the gene pool over thousands of years. The process will be slow, but it will happen (this is not the same as saying
schizophrenia
itself can be eliminated, since it is highly polygenic and the pool of risk genes is not static). Let’s say schizophrenia is associated with a 50% loss of reproductive fitness in 1% of the population (and there is no offsetting benefit in the rest of the population), then it would take roughly 180 generations to cut the rate in half and about 560 generations to reduce it to one-tenth of its original value (Mitteroecker & Merola, 2024). We’ve had a comparable number of generations since the Neolithic era, but as far as we know, the prevalence of schizophrenia has not decreased in the manner anticipated. At the same time, we do not have evidence for ongoing positive selection for schizophrenia risk alleles; in fact, schizophrenia alleles appear to be under negative selection at present, although evidence suggests many have been positively selected in the evolutionary past.
One proposed solution is to think of schizophrenia in terms of cliff-edged fitness functions, a hypothesis originally applied to schizophrenia by Randolph Nesse
in 2004
, and subsequently formalized by Philipp Mitteroecker and Giuseppe Pierpaolo Merola. As Nesse describes it succinctly, “I recognized that traits with an asymmetric fitness function are special; they give greater and greater advantages up to a point where the system fails and fitness falls off a cliff edge.”
In the case of schizophrenia, it can be hypothesized that certain cognitive, linguistic, or social traits increase fitness and are positively selected by evolution but lead to catastrophic consequences when expressed beyond a critical threshold. The model envisions a continuous, heritable trait that enhances reproductive fitness up to a point, beyond which it sharply decreases. Natural selection stabilizes the trait just below the cliff, but a small minority overshoot and suffer a dramatic fitness loss.
Fitness landscapes and cliff-edged functions
Biologists often rely on the metaphor of a fitness landscape to visualize how traits evolve under natural selection. Picture a three-dimensional terrain where different trait values correspond to different elevations of reproductive success. For some traits, like bird wing length, fitness peaks at an intermediate value, producing gently sloped hills. Wings that are too long or too short come with disadvantages that make birds less likely to survive environmental challenges. The population, under stabilizing selection, gravitates toward that middle ground, where fitness is maximized. This pattern extends to behavioral traits. Consider rabbits: those that take too many risks may be eaten by predators, while overly cautious ones may not forage enough to survive. The highest fitness lies in a temperate zone—moderate boldness, enough to eat but not enough to die. Natural selection nudges the population mean toward that sweet spot, but mutation and individual variability still produce outliers on either end, who fare worse as a result.
In certain cases, fitness continues to increase as a trait is pushed in one direction. Then, beyond a threshold, fitness plummets. Breeding racehorses illustrates this point. Selecting for speed led to increasingly longer, thinner leg bones. Thinner bones are also more likely to fracture. Selective breeding pushes the population of racehorses right to the edge of the cliff. The result is faster horses, yes, but also legs so fragile that a single misstep by the horse in a race can
44408286.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了精神分裂症在进化中的持久性问题。尽管精神分裂症是一种降低生育可能性的残疾精神疾病，但其终生患病率仍约为全球人口的1%。传统进化假说无法充分解释这一点。文章引用了Randolph Nesse的“悬崖边缘适应功能”假说，以及2024年Mitteroecker和Merola的论文，提出精神分裂症可能与某些认知、语言或社交特质的过度表达有关。这些特质在达到临界点前能提高适应性，但一旦超过该点，则会导致灾难性后果。自然选择使这些特质稳定在悬崖边缘之下，但少数个体可能越过临界点，导致适应性急剧下降。这种模型将精神分裂症视为进化过程中“悬崖边缘”现象的结果。

data.author: nradov
data.article_summary: 2024年10月19日，一颗价值5亿美元的Intelsat-33e卫星在印度洋上空爆炸，分裂成至少20块碎片，加入到地球周围约1.4万吨的太空垃圾中。由于卫星发射成本下降，而保险费用飙升，越来越多的运营商选择不为其卫星投保。这导致更多廉价卫星被快速发射，但也更容易损坏并成为新的太空垃圾，加剧了低地球轨道的拥堵问题。目前，地球上空有12,787颗卫星，但只有约300颗投保。欧洲和英国法律要求卫星必须投保，而美国公司如SpaceX通过可重复使用的火箭降低了发射成本，且通常不为其在轨卫星购买保险。太空保险市场自1965年兴起，但近年来由于损失超过保费，一些保险公司已退出该市场。

44409386.article_content:
An illustration of debris in orbit around Earth
(Image credit: Getty Images)
Airplane passengers crossing the Indian Ocean who peered out their windows on Oct. 19, 2024, might have seen what looked like a fast-moving star suddenly flash and fade. Above their heads, a $500 million satellite was exploding.
Operators
confirmed the destruction of the Intelsat-33e satellite
two days later. There was a bright flash as the satellite's fuel ignited, followed by the flickering of the debris cloud as it fragmented into
at least 20 pieces
. Those satellite parts are now zooming around Earth, along with around
14,000 tonnes
of space debris. The satellite wasn't insured.
As space junk increases, more operators are choosing to launch without any insurance at all. To compensate, companies are cutting back on the cost of
satellites
and launching more of them at faster rates, thus creating a feedback loop as the cheaper satellites break up more easily and add to the problem.
You may like
Satellites are polluting Earth's atmosphere with heavy metals. Could refueling them in orbit help?
ESA's new documentary paints worrying picture of Earth's orbital junk problem
Scientists chased a falling spacecraft with a plane to understand satellite air pollution
"I don't think it's sustainable," said
Massimiliano Vasile
, an aerospace engineer and professor at the University of Strathclyde Glasgow.
Behind the predicament are two vectors moving in opposite directions: The cost of launching satellites is falling, while the cost of insuring them continues to soar.
Even as
record-low-cost launches
are improving internet coverage and cell service, they're worsening the space junk problem.
Low Earth orbit
, where most communications satellites are circling, is becoming increasingly crowded.
Satellite insurance, meanwhile, has never been more expensive. 2023 was likely the worst ever for the market, with
reports
suggesting satellite insurers faced loss claims of more than $500 million. 2024 may have been even worse, according to
Insurance Insider
.

Breaking space news, the latest updates on rocket launches, skywatching events and more!
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
Satellite operators are responding predictably, by foregoing coverage. There are 12,787 satellites above the Earth as of the time of publication, according to the website
Orbiting Now
, which tracks active satellites, but only about 300 are actually insured for in-orbit accidents,
David Wade
, an underwriter at Atrium Space Insurance Consortium, told
Data Center Dynamics
.
European and UK operators are
legally required
to insure their satellites, which puts them at a cost disadvantage compared with India, China, Russia and the
U.S
. American companies such as
SpaceX
have also been able to reduce launch costs because of reusable rocket parts. Europe’s upcoming
Ariane 6
rocket program, for example, is expected to cost between $80-120 million
per launch
, compared with SpaceX’s Starship program which is anticipated to cost between $2-10 million per launch because of its reusable rockets.
In the U.S., launchers are required by
law
to procure liability insurance for launch, but once the satellite is in orbit, insurance is no longer needed. SpaceX, for example, is
self-insured
, meaning it seeks third-party insurance for almost none of its
Starlink satellites
.
"Typically, the launch cover is literally just for that [launch] stage, and once a satellite gets into orbit, you are off risk," said
Steve Evans
, owner of insurance data provider
Artemis
(which is unaffiliated with NASA's lunar program of the same name). The satellite "either makes it, or it doesn't," he told
Space.com.
This NASA graphic depicts the amount of space junk currently orbiting Earth. The debris field is based on data from NASA's Orbital Debris Program Office.
(Image credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center/JSC)
The space insurance market began in 1965, when Lloyds Bank
insured Intelsat I,
which broadcast the
Apollo 11
moon landing. The first known satellite failures
occurred in 1984
, though some later recovered, including the
$87 million
Intelsat 5 ($2.82 billion in today’s money).
The industry has generally hovered around a 5% failure rate since 2000, with Data Center Dynamics
reporting
that there have been only 165 claims for more than $10 million across the history of the industry.
The
2019 failure of a military observation satellite
for the United Arab Emirates, called the Vega rocket, led to $411 million in claims — the largest such loss in history, Reuters
reported
. That year, total satellite insurance losses became greater than insurance premiums for the first time, according to
Bloomberg
. Insurers were hoping to claw that money back in following years, but Reuters reported in
2021
that Assure Space and AmTrust Financial were both stopping insurance due to collisions.

data.title: Astronomers Detected a Mysterious Radio Burst from a Dead NASA Satellite
data.author: cratermoon
data.article_summary: 澳大利亚科学家去年探测到一段神秘的射电爆发信号，最初以为是快速射电暴（FRB）。但进一步分析发现，信号来自1964年发射的美国失效卫星Relay 2。该卫星自1967年以来已停止运作，爆发信号可能是由于静电放电或微流星体撞击导致。研究发表在尚未 peer-reviewed 的arXiv上，指出这种现象有助于未来监测太空中的静电放电，并保护卫星免受损害。

44406859.article_content:
Relay 2 was an American communications satellite launched in 1964.
NASA
Last year, Australian scientists picked up a mysterious burst of radio waves that briefly appeared brighter than all other signals in the sky. Now, the researchers have discovered the blast didn’t come from a celestial object, but a defunct satellite orbiting Earth.
When the team at the
Australian Square Kilometer Array Pathfinder
(ASKAP), a system of 36 radio telescopes in Western Australia, detected the 30-nanosecond pulse last June, they thought they were looking at a
fast radio burst
(FRB). These powerful flashes of radio waves often come from
highly dense objects
like neutron stars, and they usually originate in distant galaxies. But further analysis revealed that the signal came from our own Milky Way.
“We got all excited, thinking maybe we’d discovered a new pulsar or some other object,” says
Clancy James
, a researcher at Australia’s Curtin University who is on the ASKAP team, to Alex Wilkins at
New Scientist
.
After taking a closer look, however, the team realized that the only viable source for the burst was NASA’s dead
Relay 2
, a short-lived satellite that hasn’t been in operation since 1967. Their findings were published in a pre-print paper on the
arXiv
server that has not yet been peer-reviewed.
The researchers also discovered that at the time of the event, the satellite was only around 2,800 miles away from Earth, which explains why the signal appeared so strong.
Fun facts: NASA's Relay 2 satellite
Relay 2 was launched in 1964, two years after its partner
Relay 1
, as an experimental communications satellite.
The two satellites were
the first used to convey the results of an American presidential election
to Europe in 1964, stating that
Lyndon B. Johnson
had won the vote.
The reason behind Relay 2’s sudden burst is not clear, but the team has come up with two potential explanations—and neither involves the satellite coming back to life like a zombie. One relates to electrostatic discharge—a build-up of electricity that can result in a sudden blast. Spacecraft get charged with electricity when they pass through plasma, and once enough charge accumulates, it can create a spark. “New spacecraft are built with materials to reduce the build-up of charge, but when Relay 2 was launched, this wasn’t well-understood,” explains James to
Space.com
’s Robert Lea. The other idea is that a micrometeorite hit the satellite, releasing a small cloud of plasma and radio waves.
Karen Aplin,
a space scientist at the University of Bristol in England who was not involved in the study, tells
New Scientist
that it would be tough to differentiate between signals produced by each of those two scenarios, because they would look very similar.
The researchers say they favor the first idea, however, because micrometeorites the size of the one that could have caused the signal are uncommon. What’s more, the former
Arecibo Observatory
detected electrostatic discharge from GPS satellites, although those bursts were longer-lasting. Still, “we don’t know,” says James to
Space.com
.
Aplin tells
New Scientist
that the research points to the usefulness of future efforts to monitor electrostatic discharges from satellites. “In a world where there is a lot of space debris and there are more small, low-cost satellites with limited protection from electrostatic discharges, this radio detection may ultimately offer a new technique to evaluate electrostatic discharges in space,” adds Aplin.
The researchers echo that sentiment to
Space.com
, adding that these discharges are difficult to monitor.
Adam Deller
, an astrophysicist at the Swinburne University of Technology in Australia and a study co-author, tells the outlet that he hopes scientists can detect more of these signals in the future and come up with a model for how electrostatic discharges occur. “It would be great if that turned out to be useful in terms of helping to avoid damage to satellites,” he adds.

data.author: Stratoscope
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：恒星接近太阳是否会对行星系统造成破坏，特别是对地球的影响

不同观点：
• Stratoscope的观点：根据新的模拟结果，接近太阳的恒星可能会导致行星碰撞，甚至将行星抛出成为流浪行星。这种天体事件可能会对地球等行星产生重大影响，威胁到行星系统的稳定性。

• dlcarrier的观点：引用了阿西莫夫的小说《Nemesis》，提到书中的情节涉及人类试图阻止一颗类似流浪恒星靠近太阳系。这表明在科幻文学中，恒星接近太阳系的概念早已存在，并被用来构建潜在的灾难性场景。

补充讨论：
- Stratoscope引用的模拟结果提供了科学依据，说明恒星接近太阳可能导致的实际天文现象及其后果。
- dlcarrier则通过引用科幻小说，将科学概念与文学作品中的情节进行类比，增加了讨论的趣味性和文化维度。
- 争议的焦点可能在于这种天文事件的实际可能性及其对地球的具体影响程度，尽管科学模拟提供了一些证据，但在现实中发生的概率和具体后果仍存在讨论空间。
- 另一个值得注意的点是科学与科幻之间的联系，科幻作品有时能预见或反映科学研究中探讨的问题。

data.title: Blackwell: Nvidia's GPU
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: Nvidia的Blackwell架构延续了其制造大型GPU的传统，其中GB202是最大的芯片，面积750mm²，拥有922亿个晶体管和192个流式多处理器（SMs）。RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell是该系列的顶级产品，配备96GB GDDR7显存，最大时钟速度为2.85GHz。相比之下，RTX 5090屏蔽了更多SMs，拥有170个SMs，32GB显存。AMD的Radeon RX 9070则较为紧凑，拥有28个WGPs和16GB显存。Blackwell通过改进设计，使得不同类型的工作负载可以更高效地重叠执行，无需像前代一样切换子通道，提升了效率。不过，由于GPC工作分配硬件未扩展，短时任务可能仍会受限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：探讨硬件性能（如晶体管数量和面积）是否能够支持实时思考的AI模型。

不同观点：
• 观点一：认为具备大面积和大量晶体管的硬件（如750mm²面积和922亿个晶体管的芯片）可以支持AI模型进行实时思考。该观点强调硬件性能与AI模型能力之间的直接关系，认为只要硬件足够强大，AI就能实现实时思考。
  - 论据：大面积和大量晶体管意味着更强的计算能力，结合良好的模型和提示，AI可以接近实时思考。
  
• 观点二：对硬件能否真正实现AI的实时思考持怀疑态度。该观点认为，即使硬件规格强大，AI的实时思考还受到算法、模型架构、数据处理速度等其他因素的限制，不仅仅是硬件问题。
  - 论据：实时思考不仅依赖于硬件性能，还涉及模型的优化程度、延迟问题以及实际应用中的动态变化等。

补充讨论：
• 一些人关注晶体管数量和芯片面积是否是决定AI实时思考能力的唯一或主要因素，提出需要综合考虑模型设计、数据处理能力和优化水平。
• 争议焦点在于“实时思考”的定义以及现有技术水平能否真正实现这种能力。部分人认为当前的AI技术，即便硬件强大，仍难以达到人类理解中的“实时思考”。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，讨论中提到的“good model and prompt”被认为是AI实现实时思考的重要条件，但具体什么样的模型和提示才算“好”并未明确。这引发了对模型设计和提示工程在实时思考中作用的进一步讨论。

44409622.article_content:
June 28, 2025
clamchowder
Leave a comment
Nvidia has a long tradition of building giant GPUs. Blackwell, their latest graphics architecture, continues that tradition. GB202 is the largest Blackwell die. It occupies a massive 750mm2 of area, and has 92.2 billion transistors. GB202 has 192 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), the closest equivalent to a CPU core on a GPU, and feeds them with a massive memory subsystem. Nvidia’s RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell features the largest GB202 configuration to date. It sits alongside the RTX 5090 in Nvidia’s lineup, which also uses GB202 but disables a few more SMs.

A high level comparison shows the scale of Nvidia’s largest Blackwell products. AMD’s RDNA4 line tops out with the RX 9070 and RX 9070XT. The RX 9070 is slightly cut down, with four WGPs disabled out of 32. I’ll be using the RX 9070 to provide comparison data.
Acknowledgement
A massive thanks to Will Killian for giving us access to his RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell system for us to test. And so, a massive thanks goes out to him for this article!
Work Distribution
GPUs use specialized hardware to launch threads across their cores, unlike CPUs that rely on software scheduling in the operating system. Hardware thread launch is well suited to the short and simple tasks that often characterize GPU workloads. Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) are the basic building block of Nvidia GPUs, and are roughly analogous to a CPU core. SMs are grouped into Graphics Processing Clusters (GPCs), which contain a rasterizer and associated work distribution hardware.
GB202 has a 1:16 SM to GPC ratio, compared to the 1:12 ratio found in Ada Lovelace’s largest AD102 die. That lets Nvidia cheaply increase SM count and thus compute throughput without needing more copies of GPC-level hardware. However, dispatches with short-duration waves may struggle to take advantage of Blackwell’s scale, as throughput becomes limited by how fast the GPC can allocate work to the SMs rather than how fast the SMs can finish them.
AMD’s RDNA4 uses a 1:8 SE:WGP ratio, so one rasterizer feeds a set of eight WGPs in a Shader Engine. WGPs on AMD are the closest equivalent to SMs on Nvidia, and have the same nominal vector lane count. RDNA4 will be easier to utilize with small dispatches and short duration waves, but it’s worth noting that Blackwell’s design is not out of the ordinary. Scaling up GPU “cores” independently of work distribution hardware is a common technique for building larger GPUs. AMD’s RX 6900XT (RDNA2) had a 1:10 SE:WGP ratio. Before that, AMD’s largest GCN implementations like Fury X and Vega 64 had a 1:16 SE:CU ratio (CUs, or Compute Units, formed the basic building block of GCN GPUs). While Blackwell does have the same ratio as those large GCN parts, it enjoys higher clock speeds and likely has a higher wave launch rate to match per-GPU-core throughput. It won’t suffer as much as the Fury X from 10 years ago with short duration waves, but GB202 will still be harder to feed than smaller GPUs.
Example from RDNA2 with pixel shader (blue) and compute (yellow) work overlapping. Blackwell is now capable of this
Although Nvidia didn’t scale up work distribution hardware, they did make improvements on Blackwell. Prior Nvidia generations could not overlap workloads of different types on the same queue. Going between graphics and compute tasks would require a “subchannel switch” and a “wait-for-idle”. That requires one task on the queue to completely finish before the next can start, even if a game doesn’t ask for synchronization. Likely, higher level scheduling hardware that manages queues exposed to host-side applications can only track state for one workload type at a time. Blackwell does away with subchannel switches, letting it more efficiently fill its shader array if applications frequently mix different work types on the same queue.
SM Frontend
Once assigned work, the SM’s frontend fetches shader program instructions and delivers them to the execution units. Blackwell uses fixed length 128-bit (16 byte) instructions, and the SM uses a two-level instruction caching setup. Both characteristics are carried forward from Nvidia’s post-Turing/Volta designs. Each of the SM’s four partitions has a private L0 instruction cache, while a L1 instruction cache is shared across the SM.
Nvidia’s long 16 byte instructions translate to high instruction-side bandwidth demands. The L0+L1 instruction caching setup is likely intended to handle those bandwidth demands while also maintaining performance with larger code footprints. Each L0 only needs to pro
